exposure: Maternal body mass index (BMI) in the first trimester (categorized as underweight, normal, overweight, obese I, obese II)
cohort: A cohort of 642 nulliparous pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who delivered singleton babies between January 2022 and July 2024.
finding: Obesity during pregnancy is associated with a significant risk for the feto-maternal dyad, with the risk of adverse outcomes increasing with increasing obesity.
mod_finding: Compared with pregnancies with a normal BMI, obese pregnancies were significantly more likely to have caesarean delivery (CD).
birth_weight: N/A (low birth weight and macrosomia were outcomes, not specific inclusion criteria for the entire cohort)
gest_age: N/A (preterm deliveries was an outcome, not a specific inclusion criterion for the entire cohort)
